# Environment-variable knobs — the declared registry

One row per declared knob, grouped by subsystem cluster. Names use the
canonical `SOVEREIGN_` prefix; every one is mirrored to `SVRNMESH_*` by
the rebrand bridge (`sovereign-contracts/src/rebrand.rs`), so both
spellings work. `status` legend: **guard** = safety/kill-switch, keep;
**shipped** = default-on product behavior; **experiment** = A/B lever,
default-off unless noted; **deprecated** = scheduled for removal.

The registry is enforced by `cargo run -p xtask -- env-gate`: a NEW env
var read anywhere in the workspace must be declared here (or in the
gate's third-party allowlist); pre-registry debt rides the shrink-only
baseline `quality/baselines/env_unregistered.txt`. The historical
dead-codepath survey lives in `docs/ENV_VAR_AUDIT.md`.

| `SOVEREIGN_FRONTDOOR_AUTO_ALLOWLIST` | unset | guard | =1/true lets the daemon SYNTHESISE a citation allowlist from the conversation on POST /v1/chat/completions -- URLs and ev-Tn-NNNN handles seen in prior role:tool messages become SAMPLER CONSTRAINTS that mask every token extending into an unlisted value. DEFAULT OFF since 2026-08-29 because running it unconditionally on the OpenAI-compatible ingress was a silent substitution (ARCH §18.3): measured against the live daemon, one https://doc.rust-lang.org link in a cargo error made that the only reachable URL, so a request to emit https://api.stripe.com/v1/charges returned the rust-lang URL at HTTP 200 with no warning; the control run without that link emitted the Stripe URL correctly. Any coding agent whose tool output mentions a URL (cargo, npm, git remote, curl) loses the ability to write any other one. The two lanes that want the constraint (deep_research/port.rs, search_gym_cmd/runner.rs) pass url_allowlist EXPLICITLY and are unaffected by this flag -- a caller-supplied allowlist has always won over the synthesis. Ledger row: sovereign/DEFAULTS_LEDGER.md. |
| `SOVEREIGN_FRONTDOOR_RESHAPE` | on | shipped | =0/false/off serves a locally-served chat turn WITHOUT the runtime reshape passes: the three request-side nudges (failure-recovery, anti-repetition, read-attractor) that append a synthetic message the client never sent, and the two response-side canonicalizers (apply_patch heredoc, absolute path) that rewrite arguments the model already emitted. Defaults ON because all five key on the Codex/opencode contract (exec_command calls, the literal 'Process exited with code N' result shape) and each was cut against a named gym fixture -- a client with a different tool vocabulary never trips them. The switch exists because they are the only remaining passes that make a locally-served turn differ from what the same model and prompt produce under bare llama.cpp, and an operator running a shared anchor node should be able to say 'serve it unmodified' without reading frontdoor.rs to learn the passes exist. Every firing logs at INFO, so ON is auditable and OFF is total. Does NOT govern promote_in_content_tool_call, which recovers a tool call the model emitted as content and would otherwise be lost. |

## corpus

| flag | default | status | purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SOVEREIGN_CORPUS_MAINTENANCE_INTERVAL_MINS` | 60 | shipped | Minutes between self-healing corpus maintenance sweeps in the daemon (crate::corpus_maintenance). Each cycle asks every corpus how many rows sit OUTSIDE its indexes — a metadata read — and compacts/folds only those past the floor. Exists because lancedb serves a query by running the index over indexed data AND flat-scanning everything appended since, which is silent, correct and progressively slower: wikipedia reached 3,955 manifest versions and 2218ms per search while the static sep stayed at 100ms. 0 disables the sweep, which lets appended corpora decay again. |
| `SOVEREIGN_CORPUS_MAINTENANCE_KEEP_VERSIONS` | 1000 | shipped | Manifest versions a corpus may retain before the maintenance sweep reclaims, regardless of age — the bound an age alone cannot provide on a continuously-appended corpus. Deliberately generous: a ceiling that catches unbounded accumulation, not a target. Reclamation still never deletes anything younger than SOVEREIGN_CORPUS_MAINTENANCE_PRUNE_DAYS, so the directory settles at whatever the corpus writes in that window rather than at this number. 0 disables the count bound and leaves age as the only limit, which is the configuration that leaked 153.9GB on wikipedia before 2026-08-31. |
| `SOVEREIGN_CORPUS_MAINTENANCE_PRUNE_DAYS` | 1 | shipped | Reader-safety floor: no dataset version younger than this is ever deleted by the maintenance sweep. Was 7 until 2026-08-31, defended as far outside any in-flight reader WHILE ALSO bounding growth; the first claim held and the second did not, and the second was the one the default carried. wikipedia writes ~850 manifest versions a day, so all 5,972 it retained were younger than seven days and the prune phase had zero eligible targets while 153.9GB of superseded fragments sat on disk. Bounding space is now SOVEREIGN_CORPUS_MAINTENANCE_KEEP_VERSIONS' job and this knob is only what it can actually guarantee. One day is still ~10^5x the longest read that holds a version open. 0 disables pruning and retains every version. |
| `SOVEREIGN_CORPUS_MAINTENANCE_UNINDEXED_FLOOR` | 5000 | shipped | Rows-outside-the-index a corpus must exceed before the daemon's maintenance sweep rewrites it. Not zero: folding an index costs seconds-to-minutes on a large corpus and a few hundred straggler rows are genuinely cheap to flat-scan; the cost only becomes visible in the thousands. |

## daemon-lifecycle

| flag | default | status | purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SOVEREIGN_ALLOW_STALE_SOLVE` | off | guard | Opts a live daemon OUT of the stale-binary refusal in `run_identity::exe_rebuilt_since_start`, the guard `solve_http.rs` consults before serving a solve. Default OFF means the guard is ARMED: `run_identity::build()` captures `exe_mtime` at daemon startup (the banner), so a newer mtime on the same path proves a build landed UNDER a running process — every verb it serves then executes code the tree no longer contains, while `doctor` and the working tree both read fresh. The failure this prices is not hypothetical: six solve attempts on 2026-09-02 were served by a pre-dawn daemon, and the symptom was a fix that "did not work" rather than anything pointing at the binary. The refusal names its own repair (`sovereign daemon restart`), which is why the guard is a refusal and not a warning — a warning on a detached daemon goes to a log nobody is reading. Set =1 (exact match; no true/on spelling) to serve anyway, for the one legitimate case: deliberate archaeology against a build you have on purpose, e.g. reproducing a report on the binary that produced it. No DEFAULTS_LEDGER row: this is an opt-OUT of an already-default-on guard, so there is no flip-to-default pending — the desired end state is the guard staying armed. |
| `SOVEREIGN_FORCE_LOCAL` | off | guard | `1` means THIS process runs the weights — the real-mode desktop harnesses and the run-local-while-a-daemon-is-up case. Implies the in-process EmbeddedDaemon, since a child daemon would contradict it, and it TAKES PRECEDENCE over SOVEREIGN_USE_SUPERVISOR. CONSTRUCTION-TIME since 2026-08-25 (TOPOLOGY Phase 10): `DaemonHost::from_env` is the one reader; `bootstrap::detect` and `supervisor_setup::is_enabled` were two independent parses of it and now read the resolved value. |
| `SOVEREIGN_HEADROOM_HARD_MB` | off | guard | Graceful self-restart floor for host memory headroom; `auto` derives half the soft threshold. Default OFF for the same reason SOVEREIGN_RSS_HARD_LIMIT_MB is: a self-SIGTERM only helps under a supervisor that relaunches (launchd KeepAlive.SuccessfulExit=false / systemd Restart=on-failure). Distinct from the inert-guard problem it was added beside — the RSS limit measured a quantity that could not reach its threshold, whereas this one is opt-in but fires on the quantity that does. The log line states explicitly that low headroom is not an accusation: headroom is shared (an unrelated gnome-shell held 12.55 GB on the measured host), and the daemon exits because it is the process that can come back cleanly, not because it is the culprit. |
| `SOVEREIGN_HEADROOM_SOFT_MB` | max(4096, 15% of RAM) | guard | Warn threshold for HOST memory headroom (MemAvailable on Linux; free+inactive+purgeable on macOS), sampled by memory_watch beside the process-RSS limits. Added 2026-08-25 because the RSS hard limit could not fire on the host it guarded: the kernel killed the daemon at anon-rss 36.4 GiB against a 36.0 GiB steady state, with `=auto` resolving to ~108 GB — six OOM kills in 24h and the guard silent through every one (note 05cbffed). RSS is the wrong noun; the exhausted resource was GTT (GPU-mapped host memory), which RSS does not count. Warn-only and always on: saying 'the box is running out' costs nothing and is the signal that was missing. The 15% default is derived, not chosen — the pre-restart daemon sat at 19.1 GB MemAvailable on a 125 GB box (15.3%), which is the regime the kills happened in. |
| `SOVEREIGN_USE_SUPERVISOR` | on | guard | Desktop kill-switch for supervised-child mode: `0`/`false` drops the daemon CHILD process and runs an in-process EmbeddedDaemon instead. Unset (and the redundant legacy `1`) means supervised child — the default since DAEMON_RESILIENCE P0.1, the W1 flip. It has nothing to do with distributed-inference workers, which is what this entry claimed until 2026-08-24. CONSTRUCTION-TIME since 2026-08-25 (TOPOLOGY Phase 10): read once by `sovereign_contracts::launch::DaemonHost::from_env`, published by the desktop's `main`, and never consulted at a point of use again. |

## deep-research

| flag | default | status | purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SOVEREIGN_DR_ALL_LEGS_SLOW` | off | experiment | MEASUREMENT ESCAPE HATCH, not a product mode: forces EVERY deep-research drafting leg onto the primary (Slow) slot instead of the measured per-leg mapping in deep_research::port::slot_for. On-form: SOVEREIGN_DR_ALL_LEGS_SLOW=1 (also true, case-insensitive); every other value, including unset, keeps the normal mapping. Why it exists: slot_for routes Round and Section to Speed::Fast, and SECTION IS THE LEG THAT WRITES THE DELIVERABLE — so a model-ceiling diagnostic that only repoints [models] primary at a larger model would leave the actual writing on the 4B and answer a question nobody asked. The diagnostic this serves is the strategy question 'is our ~11-point gap to AIQ our ARCHITECTURE or our MODEL?': run the pipeline unchanged with a large model on every leg, and if the score approaches the bar the architecture is sound and we are model-limited, while if it barely moves the architecture is the bottleneck and model size will not save us. Cost when on: the Fast slot's ~5x speedup is given up on the two volume legs (measured 13.46s vs 68.95s per call, 2026-08-24), so runs are materially slower. Shares its on-form parser (port::pin_requested) with SOVEREIGN_DR_PIN_SAMPLING so there is one answer to 'what counts as on'. Reversal condition + evidence: sovereign/DEFAULTS_LEDGER.md. |
| `SOVEREIGN_DR_AUDIT_BATCH_LOCATE` | off | experiment | The deep-research audit's LOCATION LOOP is batched: one triage generation over the PINNED evidence window shortlists which chunks are worth a calibrated per-span call, instead of paying one calibrated call per candidate chunk. On-form: SOVEREIGN_DR_AUDIT_BATCH_LOCATE=1 (also true, case-insensitive); every other value, including unset, keeps the per-span loop. WHY IT EXISTS: measured on the pin-validate flight (research/deep-research/arms/runs-pin-validate/pinned-1.log), 328 claim audits took 102.5 minutes and 35 of them - the 11% that reached the location loop - consumed 90.6 of those minutes, 88% of the audit, at ~130s each; the other 285 short-circuited earlier and averaged 1.85s. Three hours per question is not shippable (operator, 2026-08-25). IT SHIPPED DEFAULT-ON AND ITS OWN FLIP CONDITION TURNED IT OFF THE SAME DAY: on the binder bed (sovereign-core/tests/binder_replay.rs) the first cut rejected 49 of 52 candidates including both chunks the calibrated register bound, converting a Passed claim with two origins into a corroboration-floor CouldNotJudge. Two causes, both fixed, neither yet re-measured: the prompt asked a STRICTER question than the calibrated judge ('does this passage support the claim ON ITS OWN') where a triage owes recall, and the window was built from claim-conditioned best-spans so it shared a prefix with nothing and cost 71,947ms of prefill per claim against the 1,613ms a pinned window costs. WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE WHEN IT IS ON: every chunk that binds has cleared SUPPORT_FLOOR on the same calibrated forced-choice register, so the triage can only ever COST support, never manufacture it - the failure direction is abstention, which is the honesty floor's (ARCH 18.3). Also unchanged: the verbatim-figure precheck, the MIN_LOCATE_SIM floor, the corroboration floor, the custody veto, the containment witness, and the chunk order supporting_chunk_ids is recorded in. Gated on candidate count (AUDIT_LOCATE_BATCH_MIN = 6). Read in exactly one place (deep_research::audit::batch_locate_enabled). Its cost is measured, not assumed, by SOVEREIGN_DR_AUDIT_LOCATE_SHADOW and by the binder bed. Reversal condition + evidence: sovereign/DEFAULTS_LEDGER.md. |
| `SOVEREIGN_DR_AUDIT_LOCATE_BUDGET` | 0 (unbounded) | experiment | drb1: caps how many CALIBRATED per-span calls one claim may spend locating its origins. On-form: a non-negative integer; 0, unset, empty or unparseable all mean UNBOUNDED, which is the pre-2026-08-26 behaviour. WHY IT IS THE LEVER: measured on the binder bed 2026-08-26, a calibrated span call costs ~2.4s and that cost is a ~360-token prefill which CANNOT be shared — the register judges one passage in isolation, which is the entire point of it, so there is no prefix family to put it in (its calls log stable_prefix_bytes=None by design). The only way to spend less is to make fewer calls. Bed claims 2 and 3 spent 50 and 14 calls to reach could-not-judge, and on the source flight only 1 of 6 loop-reaching claims passed at all, so most of that spend buys an abstention. Composes with SOVEREIGN_DR_AUDIT_LOCATE_EARLY_EXIT, and depends on it for legitimacy: best-first cosine ordering is what makes a bound defensible, because the candidates most likely to bind are judged first and a claim whose origins exist is expected to find them inside the budget. IT IS NOT A SILENT TRUNCATION: a claim that exhausts its budget without reaching the corroboration floor carries 'SEARCH BOUNDED: stopped after N calibrated call(s) of M candidate(s)' in its own reason string, so the record distinguishes 'we looked at everything this claim could rest on' from 'we stopped after N' (ARCH 18.3). THE RISK IT TAKES, stated plainly: a claim whose two binding origins rank below the budget in cosine order loses a Passed verdict it would otherwise have earned. That is a comprehensiveness cost against a latency gain and it is exactly what the binder bed's `fast` arm measures before any flip. Read in exactly one place (deep_research::audit::locate_call_budget). Reversal condition + evidence: sovereign/DEFAULTS_LEDGER.md. |
| `SOVEREIGN_DR_AUDIT_LOCATE_EARLY_EXIT` | off | experiment | drb1: the audit's location loop judges its located spans in DESCENDING COSINE ORDER and stops as soon as the claim has reached CORROBORATION_FLOOR (2) distinct origins. On-form: SOVEREIGN_DR_AUDIT_LOCATE_EARLY_EXIT=1 (also true, case-insensitive); every other value, including unset, visits every candidate. VERDICT-IDENTICAL BY CONSTRUCTION: the loop stops only at the moment the claim has ALREADY cleared the floor, which is exactly the condition under which it passes, so nothing found later could change Passed into anything else; a claim that never reaches the floor still visits every candidate exactly as before. The cosine is already computed by stage 2 and is free — ordering by it is what makes the exit land on the strongest origins rather than the lowest-numbered chunks. WHY IT EXISTS: measured 2026-08-26 on the binder bed, the batched triage cut a passing claim's calibrated calls from 52 to 27 but that is only ~1.55x on the warm per-claim term (127s -> 82s), and the claim's two binding origins (ev-25, ev-30) were found part-way through an unordered sweep — best-first with an exit at the floor stops after finding them. WHAT IT DOES CHANGE, and why it is its own flag rather than a free rider on the batch: supporting_chunk_ids and corroboration.support_chunks get SMALLER, because the record then carries the origins that SETTLED the claim rather than every chunk that would have bound. That is a real change to what the deliverable can cite per claim and it is measured separately (binder_replay arm `early`) before any flip. Read in exactly one place (deep_research::audit::locate_early_exit_enabled). Reversal condition + evidence: sovereign/DEFAULTS_LEDGER.md. |
| `SOVEREIGN_DR_AUDIT_LOCATE_SHADOW` | off | experiment | MEASUREMENT MODE for SOVEREIGN_DR_AUDIT_BATCH_LOCATE, not product behaviour: issues the calibrated per-span judge for the spans the batched triage REJECTED as well, and counts how many of them the calibrated register would have bound (`shadow_lost` on the `t5 binder` INFO event, plus a WARN whenever it is non-zero). On-form: SOVEREIGN_DR_AUDIT_LOCATE_SHADOW=1 (also true, case-insensitive); every other value, including unset, leaves the rejected spans unjudged. Why it exists: with the triage on and the shadow off, a rejected span is never judged and its lost support is unobservable BY CONSTRUCTION — the same blindness that made the grounding ladder's safety argument unmeasurable until SOVEREIGN_GATE_CLAIM_SEARCH_SHADOW existed. This is the only configuration in which the batch's real cost can be priced, and the promotion evidence for leaving it default-on is a bank-level shadow_lost of zero (or a named, accepted rate). Cost when on: the FULL pre-batch call count plus the triage generation, so a run under the shadow is slower than the loop it replaced — a measurement run, never a product one. Read in exactly one place (deep_research::audit::locate_shadow_enabled). Reversal condition + evidence: sovereign/DEFAULTS_LEDGER.md. |
| `SOVEREIGN_DR_COMPOSED_REPORT` | ON (set =0 to restore the claim-ledger render) | shipped | drb1-t5: the deep-research deliverable is COMPOSED (one section per planned sub-question over the whole merged evidence window, plus a closing synthesis — AIQ teardown §1.6/§6.3) instead of being rebuilt from atomised claim rows. On-form: SOVEREIGN_DR_COMPOSED_REPORT=1 (also true, case-insensitive); every other value, including unset, leaves the claim-ledger render in place. Read in exactly one place (deep_research::composed_report_enabled). Reversal condition + evidence: sovereign/DEFAULTS_LEDGER.md. |
| `SOVEREIGN_DR_PIN_SAMPLING` | off | experiment | MEASUREMENT HARNESS, not product behaviour: pins the deep-research writer's sampling to greedy (temperature 0.0, top_p 1.0) across EVERY drafting leg — draft, query-rewrite and plan-subquestions — so an A/B measures the lever instead of the sampler. On-form: SOVEREIGN_DR_PIN_SAMPLING=1 (also true, case-insensitive); every other value, including unset, keeps production sampling (0.4 on draft/plan, 0.3 on rewrite). Why it exists: the judge is pinned greedy (one judge instrument, one sampling pin) while the writer was not, so we pinned the instrument and left the subject free. Measured 2026-08-25 on the task-69 replay bed with evidence held constant, THREE runs at identical configuration scored 42.21 / 41.99 / 48.91 — a 6.92-point spread, matching the 7.56-point pipeline spread measured earlier. Every A/B run against that bed tested a 2-3 point lever with n=2 and therefore could not resolve; detecting 2-3 points against that spread needs ~15-20 reps per arm, which at ~22 min per rep is a week per question. WHAT IT DOES NOT FIX: a pinned writer is a slightly different writer than the sampled one we ship, so a lever measured under the pin still needs confirming unpinned before it lands — the trade is deliberate, since an underpowered measurement of the real writer resolves nothing at all. Reversal condition + evidence: sovereign/DEFAULTS_LEDGER.md. |
| `SOVEREIGN_DR_REPORT_ARCHITECTURE` | ON (set =0 to restore the pipeline-shaped deliverable) | shipped | drb1-r8: the deliverable carries the ARCHITECTURE of a report - its own title, an executive summary that answers the question first, and a Conclusion - instead of the shape of the pipeline that produced it. On-form: SOVEREIGN_DR_REPORT_ARCHITECTURE=1 (also true, case-insensitive); every other value, including unset, leaves the composed report byte-identical. Requires SOVEREIGN_DR_COMPOSED_REPORT=1; composes with SOVEREIGN_DR_REPORT_OUTLINE, which decides WHICH sections exist while this decides what surrounds them. Why it exists, diagnosed from the judge's own per-criterion scores across 25 task-69 records rather than guessed: the criteria we lose most are Breadth and Depth of MCP Protocol Description (ours 6.12 vs the reference article's 9.36, in 25 of 25 draws), Logical Structure and Coherent Flow of Argumentation (6.60 vs 9.50), Formatting Layout and Typographical Consistency (6.98 vs 9.48) and Paragraph Cohesion Sentence Fluency and Conciseness (6.80 vs 9.02) - six of our seven worst criteria are readability, which is a property of how the article is WRITTEN, not of what was retrieved. Three named structural causes, each addressed here: (1) compose_report's H1 was the user's raw prompt sentence (synthesize.rs, the format! at the end of compose_report), so the deliverable announced itself as a machine artifact; a planned title replaces it. (2) There was no summary and the report closed on 'Synthesis and Assessment' - the pipeline's own vocabulary; an executive summary written LAST and read FIRST answers the question in its first two sentences, and the closing section is titled Conclusion. (3) OUTLINE_MAX capped the plan at 8 sections, so a question naming two subjects could not afford a section for the second one - which is exactly the MCP deficit above; the cap is 12 when this is on. The cap is ONE decider (synthesize::outline_max) read by both the prompt that asks for n sections and the parser that admits them, so the writer can never be asked for 12 and admitted for 8; watched red in synthesize::tests::the_section_cap_is_one_decider_for_the_prompt_and_the_parser. WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE WHEN IT IS ON: the citation contract and therefore the gate. The title and summary add no claims of their own - the summary is told to assert nothing the report does not already establish and to reuse the [Source: ev-N] handles already used below, and both are composed BEFORE the audit pass, so every sentence they carry faces the same gate as the sections. A refused title (outside 20-160 chars) falls back to the question and a failed summary lands the report without one, both NAMED in the trace, never silently (ARCH 18.3); watched red in synthesize::tests::the_title_parser_refuses_what_is_not_a_title. Cost: two extra draft calls per run (title, summary). Read in exactly one place (deep_research::report_architecture_enabled). Reversal condition + evidence: sovereign/DEFAULTS_LEDGER.md. |
| `SOVEREIGN_DR_REPORT_OUTLINE` | ON (set =0 to restore the search frontier) | shipped | drb1-r5: the composed report's sections come from a PLANNED OUTLINE rather than from the acquisition frontier. On-form: SOVEREIGN_DR_REPORT_OUTLINE=1 (also true, case-insensitive); every other value, including unset, keeps one-section-per-sub-question. Requires SOVEREIGN_DR_COMPOSED_REPORT=1 — there is no outline without a composed deliverable to structure. Why it exists: compose_report wrote one section per planned sub-question, and those come from the planner prompt that deliberately asks for the measure or statistic each implies, so the task-69 web arm shipped sections titled `Count of distinct error handling states defined in the A2A message schema`. Three of that arm's four largest weighted losses were structural with 98 sources in hand — the judge wrote `Article 2 dedicates Section III to MCP ... Article 1 lacks a comprehensive standalone explanation` (5.0 vs 9.0), `Article 2 has a dedicated Section VI (Interplay and Relationship)` (6.0 vs 9.5), `Article 2 explicitly maps problems to solutions in Section IX` (6.5 vs 9.5) — and a fourth said the granularity costs insight, the worst of our four dimensions. The outline is planned over the evidence actually gathered so it cannot promise sections nothing supports; the prompt describes a shape and never an answer. An unusable outline (fewer than 2 briefed sections) REFUSES and the loop falls back to the frontier with the fallback named in the trace, never silently. Cost: one extra Slow-slot draft call per run. Read in exactly one place (deep_research::report_outline_enabled). Reversal condition + evidence: sovereign/DEFAULTS_LEDGER.md. |
| `SOVEREIGN_DR_REPORT_SECTION_EVIDENCE` | off | experiment | drb1-r9: how much of the evidence window ONE section's writer is shown. On-form: SOVEREIGN_DR_REPORT_SECTION_EVIDENCE=1 (also true, case-insensitive); every other value, including unset, keeps 8 passages at a 3-per-source cap. Requires SOVEREIGN_DR_COMPOSED_REPORT=1. Deliberately SEPARATE from SOVEREIGN_DR_REPORT_ARCHITECTURE: that flag decides the deliverable's shape, this one decides how much evidence stands behind each part of it, and an arm that moves both cannot tell them apart. Why it exists, measured on the task-69 control flight dr-1787742429 rather than reasoned: the evidence window held 46 chunks and 1,060,308 characters, MCP material appears in 40 of those 46 chunks and the MCP primitives in 41 - so ACQUISITION IS NOT THE CONSTRAINT - yet at SECTION_PASSAGES=8 x PASSAGE_CHARS=1400 one section's writer sees 11,200 chars, 1.06% of the window, and eight sections see 8.5% between them. The 11,345-word report that came out cites 22 of the 46 available sources and contains no section describing MCP, which is our single worst RACE criterion in 25 of 25 draws. The writer is not failing to use the evidence; it is not being shown it. What this turns on: 28 passages per section at a 5-per-source cap - NOT a guess: it RESTORES the configuration the composed report's own quality number was measured at. compose_report was ported to Rust in a50d2fdf3 from the Python prototype arms/lab/compose2.py, whose commit message records that the 44.40 composite standing in for its quality was measured by that prototype; the prototype chunks passages identically (size=1400, overlap=200), ranks by the same cosine, applies the same per-source cap, and used k=28 repeat_cap=5, recording evidence_chars_per_section = k*1400 = 39200 in its own manifest. The port shipped 8 and 3 - 11200 chars, a 3.5x cut - and no commit, note or ledger row records that as a decision. Commit 14ddccf49 later OBSERVED the consequence and responded with the research-notes flag rather than restoring the number, so the shipped Rust path has never run at the configuration whose measured quality justified building it. Both knobs move together through ONE decider (synthesize::section_evidence_budget) because widening the count while holding the cap at 3 would fill the new room from new SOURCES only - the opposite of what a section needing depth on one subject requires, since a spec page carries its detail across consecutive passages; watched red in synthesize::tests::the_section_evidence_budget_widens_both_knobs_together. WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE WHEN IT IS ON: the citation contract and therefore the gate. The passages are the same passages, drawn from the same window by the same cosine ranker with the same ev-N handles; only how many of them the writer sees changes. No new evidence enters, nothing is re-chunked, and the audit locates spans exactly as before. Cost: roughly 3x the section-writer prefill (11k -> 34k chars per section prompt) and no extra calls. Read in exactly one place (deep_research::report_section_evidence_enabled). Reversal condition + evidence: sovereign/DEFAULTS_LEDGER.md. |
| `SOVEREIGN_DR_RESEARCH_NOTES` | off | experiment | drb1-r4: the composed report's sections are written from DISTILLED FINDINGS produced by one researcher worker per sub-question, instead of from the top-SECTION_PASSAGES retrieved passages. On-form: SOVEREIGN_DR_RESEARCH_NOTES=1 (also true, case-insensitive); every other value, including unset, leaves the passage path in place. Requires SOVEREIGN_DR_COMPOSED_REPORT=1 — notes feed the composer's sections, so with the composed report off there is no writer to feed and this flag does nothing. Why it exists: our AIQ teardown (research/deep-research/aiq-teardown.md §1.3) attributes that system's DRB-II InfoRecall lead (49.23, above o3, Gemini-3-Pro and Grok) to handing the writer structured research notes rather than raw passages; ours showed each section eight passages by cosine, so on the logged task-69 flight a 38-chunk window reached the writer eight chunks at a time. What does NOT change when it is on: the citation contract and therefore the gate. A finding carries the ev-N handles of the window chunks it rests on, the writer cites those same handles, and the audit locates spans exactly as before; a finding citing an id the window does not hold is REFUSED WHOLE and recorded with its reason, never admitted with the bad id dropped (that would re-attribute the claim to a chunk that never supported it — watched red in deep_research::notes::tests). A sub-question whose findings are all refused falls back to passages, named in the trace, never composed from nothing. Cost: one extra Slow-slot draft call per sub-question per run. Read in exactly one place (deep_research::research_notes_enabled). Reversal condition + evidence: sovereign/DEFAULTS_LEDGER.md. |
| `SOVEREIGN_DR_SECTION_CONTEXT` | off | experiment | Each section's writer is shown the report's full outline with its own position marked, instead of composing in isolation. On-form: SOVEREIGN_DR_SECTION_CONTEXT=1 (also true, case-insensitive); every other value, including unset, leaves the section prompt BYTE-IDENTICAL to the one the evidence curve was measured on. Requires SOVEREIGN_DR_COMPOSED_REPORT=1. Deliberately SEPARATE from SOVEREIGN_DR_REPORT_ARCHITECTURE: that flag decides the deliverable's SHAPE (title, executive summary, closing), this one decides whether a section knows it is PART of one, and an arm that moves both cannot tell them apart. Why it exists, measured on bed dr-1787807617 (task 69) rather than reasoned: after the section-evidence default moved to 16/4, readability is the ONLY RACE dimension still behind the reference (-1.21 at the default, against +0.42 comprehensiveness, +1.12 insight, +0.60 instruction-following) AND the only dimension the evidence budget does not move (7.86 -> 8.21 across a 7.5x increase in evidence). The judge's objection is a single sentence: the report has 'a somewhat fragmented structure with many short sections that jump between topics ... reads like a collection of research findings rather than a single narrative arc'. THE OBVIOUS CAUSE WAS FLOWN AND REFUTED: a 10-section outline against the same window (via COMPOSE_SECTIONS, planned by production plan_outline) left Logical Structure at EXACTLY 8.5 - unchanged from the 22-section control - while costing 0.61 overall and dropping Formatting 9.5 -> 8.5. Section COUNT is not the cause. What is left is the prompt: synthesize.rs hands a section writer the question, its own sub-question, its evidence and a word budget, and NOTHING about its neighbours, so every section is composed in isolation no matter how many there are - ten isolated sections read as disjointed as twenty. This flag prepends the ordered section list with an arrow on the writer's own entry and instructs it to assume the reader has read what is above and will read what is below. WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE WHEN IT IS ON: the citation contract and therefore the gate. No new evidence enters, no passage is re-ranked, no extra model call is made - only the prompt's preamble grows, by roughly 40 characters per planned section (about 800 on a 20-section plan, ~3.5% of a 16x4 section prompt). Read in exactly one place (deep_research::section_context_enabled). Reversal condition + evidence: sovereign/DEFAULTS_LEDGER.md. |
| `SOVEREIGN_DR_SECTION_PASSAGES` | unset (the boolean SOVEREIGN_DR_REPORT_SECTION_EVIDENCE decides: 8 off, 28 on) | experiment | drb1-r9 sweep knob: the NUMBER of passages one section's writer is shown, overriding whatever the boolean flag chose. On-form: a positive integer; unset, empty, unparseable and ZERO all mean 'not set' and fall through — a zero is never honoured as a budget of nothing, which would collapse every section to no evidence and still emit a plausible report (ARCH 18.3). WHY A NUMBER AND NOT JUST THE BOOLEAN: 28/5 is one point, not an optimum — 28 x PASSAGE_CHARS 1400 is still only ~2.8% of a ~995-passage window — and the measured arm (2026-08-26, task 69, both cells pinned) put the lever at +3.67 overall (control 47.23 -> wide 50.90) with comprehensiveness leading at +5.79, which is a LEAD at 1.24 sd and n=1, not a resolved optimum. Finding the knee needs the knob swept, and a boolean cannot sweep. Resolves through the SAME decider as the boolean (synthesize::section_evidence_budget), so the ranker that picks passages and the cap that shapes the pick can still never be set from different rules (10.6). Read by tests/compose_replay.rs, which replays the production compose_report against a frozen compose-input.json in ~12 min per arm instead of the ~96-min flight. Reversal condition + evidence: sovereign/DEFAULTS_LEDGER.md. |
| `SOVEREIGN_DR_SECTION_SOURCE_CAP` | unset (the boolean decides: 3 off, 5 on) | experiment | drb1-r9 sweep knob: the PER-SOURCE cap on a section's passages, overriding whatever the boolean flag chose. Same on-form and same zero-is-not-a-budget rule as SOVEREIGN_DR_SECTION_PASSAGES, and the same single decider. WHY IT IS SWEPT SEPARATELY: widening the count while holding the cap narrow fills the new room from new SOURCES only, which is the opposite of what a section needing depth on one subject requires (a spec page carries its detail across consecutive passages) — so the two knobs interact and a curve over one at a fixed other is a different experiment from a curve over both. Measured note: at want=8/cap=3 the cap is not binding (8 passages need only 3 distinct sources) and at 28/5 it needs 6, against ~49-60 sources available — so on the 2026-08-26 arm the cap was almost certainly NOT doing the work, and the +3.67 belongs to volume. That is an inference from the selection code (synthesize::rank_passages), not a measurement, and sweeping this knob is how it gets one. Reversal condition + evidence: sovereign/DEFAULTS_LEDGER.md. |
| `SOVEREIGN_DR_TARGET_WORDS` | unset — the length DERIVES from the evidence each section receives (synthesize::section_word_budget). Setting a positive integer pins a total and divides it by the section count, which is the pre-2026-08-27 behaviour, kept because a length A/B needs both arms at one length under one binary. | experiment | drb1-r6: overrides the composed deliverable's TARGET TOTAL word count, from which the per-section budget is derived (TARGET_REPORT_WORDS / sections, clamped 300-1400). On-form: a positive integer; unset, empty, unparseable or 0 all keep the 9000 default — a bad value is never a silent zero, which would collapse every section to SECTION_WORDS_MIN and silently ship a stub. Why it exists: the matched-length outline A/B (2026-08-25) landed 11,375-11,837 words against a 9,000 ask — the writer overshoots by ~26% — and the shorter pre-fix control at 9,219 words scored 47.52 against that arm's 42.10, with every shorter run beating every longer one. Testing whether shorter is genuinely better requires BOTH lengths under ONE binary in one session; editing the const between arms reintroduces the cross-binary, cross-day confound that is exactly what makes the current 5.42-point separation a lead rather than a result. UNRESOLVED CONFOUND this flag is meant to help separate: the judge reads our article AND the ~9,000-word reference in a single prompt (~30k tokens for an 11.8k-word article), so a length effect may belong to the JUDGE's attention over a longer prompt rather than to the writer — validate the instrument before crediting the result (ARCH_PRINCIPLES §18.4). Read in exactly one place (synthesize::target_report_words). Reversal condition + evidence: sovereign/DEFAULTS_LEDGER.md. |
| `SOVEREIGN_DR_WRITER_CONTRACT_V2` | off | experiment | drb1-r7: the section writer sees GRADED evidence and is told what each grade obliges, instead of a flat list it must weigh unaided. On-form: SOVEREIGN_DR_WRITER_CONTRACT_V2=1 (also true, case-insensitive); every other value, including unset, keeps the flat evidence block and the v1 contract. Why it exists: AIQ's writer prompt steers synthesis by a per-note evidence_judgment - high-scoring notes are anchors, medium ones support and nuance, low ones are for gaps, caveats and conflicts (aiq clone, src/aiq_agent/agents/deep_researcher/prompts/writer.j2, Synthesis Contract). WE ALREADY COMPUTE THAT GRADE ON BOTH EVIDENCE PATHS AND THEN DISCARD IT: Finding carries usefulness (0-100) and notes::findings_block sorts by it before dropping it, and synthesize::rank_passages returns passages in descending cosine order which the evidence block then flattens - so the writer receives an ordered list and is never told what the ordering means. This surfaces the grade the pipeline already earned and states the obligation that goes with it. It ALSO appends the four writer.j2 obligations v1 lacks, checked line by line against that file rather than recalled: how to use the grade, name consensus and combine complementary evidence, inference that is licensed but marked and confidence-weighted, and when a table earns its place (units, dates, ranges; never a table restating the prose). v1 ALREADY holds cross-synthesis, evaluate-don't-report, conflict surfacing, developed paragraphs, detail retention and err-toward-more, and v2 deliberately does NOT repeat them - a duplicated obligation is a prompt arguing with itself, watched red in synthesize::tests::the_v2_extra_ports_what_v1_lacks_and_does_not_repeat_it. WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE WHEN IT IS ON: the citation contract and therefore the gate. Grades are advisory prose in the prompt; they do not alter which chunks are in the window, which ev-N handles exist, what the audit locates, the corroboration floor, the custody veto or the containment witness. The grade bands straddle DEFAULT_USEFULNESS (50) so a finding the worker declined to score lands in SUPPORT and is never read as a judgement in either direction (ARCH 18.3), and a section with fewer than 3 passages grades every one ANCHOR so the contract can never tell a thin section not to build on the only evidence it has. Targets insight -15.20 and readability -11.93 (note bdf94683); the model rung was measured and does not pay (note 403a218a), which is why the next lever is the prompt contract. Cost: zero extra calls - the grade is already computed. Read in exactly one place (deep_research::writer_contract_v2_enabled). Reversal condition + evidence: sovereign/DEFAULTS_LEDGER.md. |

## dev-gates

| flag | default | status | purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SOVEREIGN_LINT_JOBS` | unset (derived from cores + free memory) | guard | Caps the cargo job fan for scripts/sovereign-lint.sh. Unset resolves through lib/cargo-jobs.sh, which budgets from cores AND free memory: `cargo check` is lighter than the test gate, but it is the same unbounded fan against the same RAM, so it obeys one budget rather than a second rule. This is the per-machine lever — a box holding a resident big model pins itself low in a shell profile; --jobs overrides it per run. |
| `SOVEREIGN_NO_COMMIT_SMELLS` | off | guard | Set to 1 to silence .claude/hooks/commit-smells.py, the PreToolUse hook that runs the model-free ARCH §15 smell gate (scripts/co-arch.py over quality/arch-probes.toml) on what a `git commit` would record and blocks the agent once per site per session. A kill-switch for a false-positive storm or a fixture-heavy commit; the nightly co-arch audit still judges the commit afterwards, so nothing is lost by opting out, only the in-session placement of the principle next to the diff. |
| `SOVEREIGN_PYTHON` | unset (first of python3.13, python3.12, python3.11, python3 on PATH) | guard | Names the interpreter scripts/co-review.sh and scripts/co-sweep.sh run their python passes under. Unset walks a fixed candidate list; when NOTHING on it resolves, both scripts SAY SO and exit rather than skipping the pass — an audit that did not run is reported, never defaulted to green (ARCH §18.3). This is the per-machine escape hatch for a host whose python lives off PATH or under a name the list does not carry. |
| `SOVEREIGN_TEST_JOBS` | unset (derived from cores + free memory) | guard | Caps the cargo job fan for scripts/sovereign-test.sh — build+link+run, the heaviest fan in the repo. Twin of SOVEREIGN_LINT_JOBS on the same lib/cargo-jobs.sh budget; --jobs overrides it per run. The resolved value is what the banner's `jobs:` line reports, so a run that self-throttled on low free memory says so instead of just being slow. |
| `SOVEREIGN_TOOLBOX` | sovereign-vulkan | guard | The toolbox container scripts/lib/release-host.sh runs native build legs inside. The default matches the container this repo's native deps (cmake, clang, vulkan) are installed in; the knob exists because the container name is a property of the HOST, not of the release. Resolution is guarded, not assumed: the driver uses `toolbox run -c $SOVEREIGN_TOOLBOX` only when the `toolbox` binary exists AND `toolbox list --containers` actually names it, so a missing or renamed container degrades loudly instead of producing a leg that silently built on the host. |

| `SOVEREIGN_ENRICH_PROGRESS` | off (human banners) | shipped | Set to `json` and `svrn enrich build` emits one `@progress {…}` line per typed EnrichProgress event on stdout instead of human banners. Set by the PARENT process, not by an operator: sovereign_tools::enrich spawns the CLI and used to rebuild the event stream by regex-matching the banners, so rewording one for a human silently froze the desktop's progress panel (TOPOLOGY §9.3). An env var rather than a flag because the parent may resolve an OLDER sovereign-cli from $PATH — an unknown flag makes that binary exit 2, while an unknown env var is ignored and the reader reports ProgressWire::Silent. Purely additive: a locator appears only where the WHOLE quote is one contiguous span of one chunk AND the join can attribute that chunk, so a corpus without section structure, without a populated join, or a quote that matched only as a partial run releases exactly the text it always did. Display-only and outside the quote marks, so it can never make a claim pass a check. =0 is the CONTROL arm for the situated lane's `cites_a_source` criterion, which was 0/7 in both arms of arm C because the answer path had nothing per-passage to name (2026-08-05). |

The single-sentence contract grounds 0/14 compound probes (measured 2x n=7, 2026-08-04) because no one sentence answers a two-part question. Flipped ON 2026-08-05 on a matched control (saltgrass_compound n=7, same HEAD/day/topology, 0 extraction failures both arms): citation releases 0->3, competence-when-present 0.14->0.43, gate-attributed misses 4->2, blatant-confab-rate 0.00 unchanged. =0 for the control arm. |

One `audit` record per pass carries the evidence window (leaf + summary chunks, labels, the extracted claim list, tau, budget); one `claim` record per decision names the MECHANISM that made it (per_claim_judge / batched / deterministic_veto / specifics_scan / identifier_sweep / exempt_self_referential), its violation probability, and any claim-conditioned passages that widened the window; one `audit_result` record closes the pass with audited/failed/ratio/zero_failure. Exists because the audit's failure verdicts were never inspectable — `dbg()` printed the claim and its vp but never the evidence it was judged against, so 'is this failure real?' could not be answered from outside the process (ARCH §18.4, validate the instrument before the result). Default unset: the records carry verbatim corpus text and the model's draft. |

The single batched prefill only amortises when it replaces enough per-claim calls — measured break-even ~6 claims (audit#1 median is exactly 6, range 3-12). |

Register replay-recalibrated (judge_replay v2 set, fc58319d): catch 0.950 / clear 1.000, zero (c)-class loss, bit-stable; measured batch support rate 53.7% on audit#1. Fires only at >= SOVEREIGN_GATE_BATCH_MIN_CLAIMS extracted claims. | `SOVEREIGN_SUFFICIENCY_CHUNKS` | 12 | experiment | How many round-0 chunks the agentic loop's sufficiency judge reads. |
| `SOVEREIGN_SURGICAL_MAX_FAILED_RATIO` | 0.5 | guard | The share of a longform draft's AUDITED claims that may fail and still be repaired by targeted surgery instead of a full 35B re-synthesis. 0.5 is derived, not tuned: the rule is 'surgery unless MOST claims fail', and a majority is more than half. Replaces SOVEREIGN_SURGICAL_MAX_FAILURES (absolute count, default 3) on 2026-08-13 — claim_budget scales the audited count with answer length, so an absolute cap inverted with length and structurally excluded longform (measured 51.2s fallback on a real desktop turn vs 1.7-2.7s when surgery engaged; NATIVE_GROUNDING_ECONOMY.md 7.3.1). Read in exactly one place (grounding/mod.rs surgical_max_failed_ratio); 0.0 forces full re-synthesis, 1.0 forces surgery, and those are the two positions the surgical calibration harness uses. Unparseable or out-of-range values warn and fall back to 0.5. Measured yield of the change over 8 warm desktop turns: 0 ms — it makes the code agree with its rationale, it did not make the query faster (ECONOMY 7.3.2). |

| flag | default | status | purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SOVEREIGN_ALLOW_INPROCESS_DISTRIBUTED_PRIMARY` | unset | guard | Override the containment guard that compute.distributed_primary arms (in-process distributed primary). *(shadows `SetupConfig.compute.distributed_primary`)* |

| `SOVEREIGN_CAPABILITY_PROBE` | on | shipped | Load-time measured capability probe for a chat slot (embedded::capabilities): prefill, generate, roll back ACROSS the decode-pass boundary, replay identical tokens, compare continuations. Establishes PartialKvVerdict by measurement instead of inferring it from the gguf arch string. =0/false/off skips it and leaves the record CouldNotJudge, which vetoes rather than defaulting to a pass. Costs ~0.3-1s per slot load. SHADOW PHASE: the verdict is recorded and logged on target `capability`; prefix_cache_gate still follows the arch ladder, so disabling this changes no answer, only observability. |
| `SOVEREIGN_CLIENT_FAIRNESS` | on | guard | Kill switch for per-principal equal share on the client inference surface (:9741 /v1/chat/completions), order serve50-identity. On: a caller already holding its share of the host's concurrency gets 503 + Retry-After while other principals are active. Off: the principal is still resolved and logged but never capped, which restores the unfair BEHAVIOUR (measured 2026-08-13: polite cohort back to 0.114x fair share, greedy at 9.0x overshoot) so the A/B is one env var rather than two builds. It does not restore the old BINARY: the layer still resolves the principal and does the accounting when off, which costs measurably under a refusal storm. See MESH_SCALE_100_USERS_1000_CORPORA.md §9.5. Does not affect peer traffic (X-Node-Id), which is rationed per node by the peer admission gate. |
| `SOVEREIGN_CLIENT_FAIR_CONCURRENCY` | 16 | shipped | Concurrency budget divided equally among ACTIVE client principals to give each one its cap (fair_share_cap in serving-policy/src/fair_sched.rs). Derived from the slot queue's own shed bound: SOVEREIGN_MAX_QUEUE_WAIT_SECS=30 at a ~1.9s turn against one decode permit, i.e. the depth at which the host is fully committed but not yet refusing. Sized there on purpose so the cap only changes WHOSE turns fill the host, never whether it sheds. A lone principal is never capped at all regardless of this value. Zero or malformed is reported and falls back to the default. |

The coalescer channel was unbounded, and FastShort takes its inflight permit AFTER the queue, so the backlog was invisible to queue.depth() and the slot's predicted-wait shed could never fire on this path — an enrichment pass that outran decode grew the queue until the process died, every caller still parked on its oneshot. Default 64 = eight full batches at n_seq_max 8; a queue deeper than that is a memory leak with a completion handler. A zero or unparseable value falls back to the default rather than producing a shed-everything channel. |

A journal is one feature's append-only metadata-only record of how it behaved on the developer's real work, under ~/.svrnmesh/journal/<stream>-<date>.jsonl (today: next-edit; the layer is feature-agnostic — sovereign-contracts/src/types/journal.rs). This is the CI/harness switch; the developer-facing opt-out is `svrn journal off`, which drops a DISABLED marker needing no daemon restart. Global env, global marker, per-stream env and per-stream marker are all read by ONE decider, JournalStream::enabled. Local write is default-ON and sending is NEVER: no network path exists in the module, and `svrn journal bundle` writes a file plus a manifest of every field in it. Ledger row: sovereign/DEFAULTS_LEDGER.md. |
| `SOVEREIGN_JOURNAL_DIR` | unset | shipped | Overrides the journal directory for every stream. Tests and operators only — unset resolves through rebrand::journal_dir() so the ~/.svrnmesh rebrand and its legacy ~/.sovereign fallback are honoured (clippy.toml's path-SSOT ban). |
| `SOVEREIGN_LOCAL_FIT_CHECK_SKIP` | unset | deprecated | Word-order twin read in the SAME fallback expression as its alias target — one knob, two spellings; scheduled to collapse onto the alias target. *(alias of `SOVEREIGN_SKIP_LOCAL_FIT_CHECK`)* |
| `SOVEREIGN_LOCAL_FIT_ENFORCE` | off | guard | Makes the local-fit gate REFUSE a load it predicts will not fit, instead of warning and loading anyway. Default OFF — the gate is ADVISORY (operator direction 2026-08-27, reversing its original posture). Why the default flipped: the gate predicts, it does not know; it estimates weights + projected KV/scratch against MemAvailable minus a heuristic reserve, and every term can be conservative — most sharply for a model that leaves a large tensor in the mmap, which is exactly the case (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, 26.8 GiB engram) where it refused a model that then loaded and served fine. The failure modes are asymmetric: a wrong REFUSAL is silent and total (the model reports unavailable and the override name appears only in a log line the operator never sees), while a wrong ADMISSION is loud and bounded (the load fails or the process dies, with the gate's full arithmetic logged immediately above it). Prefer the loud one. Set this to 1 on an unattended host that would rather stay up than crash — the right choice for a server, the wrong default for someone running a model on their own machine. The predicate itself is unchanged and still logs every term; only what the placement DOES with the verdict changed. Distinct from SOVEREIGN_LOCAL_FIT_CHECK_SKIP / SOVEREIGN_SKIP_LOCAL_FIT_CHECK, which skip the computation entirely and therefore also silence the forecast. Does NOT affect the per-device worker fit gate (SOVEREIGN_SKIP_PER_DEVICE_FIT), which still refuses: an overflowing shard aborts a REMOTE peer mid-graph, which is neither loud nor bounded on the machine that has to diagnose it. |
| `SOVEREIGN_MAX_QUEUE_WAIT_SECS` | 30 | shipped | Ceiling on how long a caller may wait SILENTLY for a model permit before the host sheds with a structured 503 + Retry-After (MESH_N4_TOPOLOGY M5). Bounds PREDICTED WAIT, not queue depth: measured 2026-08-06, an identical depth of 8 cost 6.2s when callers shared a prompt prefix and 90.7s when they did not. =0 restores the pre-M5 unbounded wait. Raise it for a hub deployment with no alternative holder, where a shed means no answer rather than a slow one. |

| `SOVEREIGN_MTP_DISABLE` | unset | guard | Kill-switch: disable multi-token-prediction speculative decoding. |
| `SOVEREIGN_MTP_DRAFT_MAX` | 3 | shipped | MTP speculative draft depth (n_draft_max). Admitted range is 1..mtp_n_rs_seq (structural cap n_rs_seq - 1: one slot of headroom for partial KV rollback on the recurrent layers). Out-of-range or unparseable values WARN and fall back to 3 — a named substitution, never silent (ARCH_PRINCIPLES §18.3). Default 3 is upstream's Qwen3.6-A3B sweet spot; the 3.8-UD A/B is order deep-research-t7c (2026-08-19). |
| `SOVEREIGN_MTP_PREFILL_TAIL_LOGITS` | off | experiment | The MTP prefill flags ONLY its final position for logits instead of every position. On-form: SOVEREIGN_MTP_PREFILL_TAIL_LOGITS=1 (also true, case-insensitive); every other value, including unset, keeps today's all-position flagging. WHY IT EXISTS: flagging every position makes n_outputs_all the whole prompt (llama-context.cpp:1700), so output_reserve sizes the logits buffer at n_vocab * n_prompt_tokens * 4 - 993,280 bytes PER PROMPT TOKEN at the qwen35 family's 248,320 vocab. Past ~3,650 tokens that exceeds this device's 4 GiB maxBufferSize, fails to pin, and falls back to a host CPU buffer that is retained at high-water until the process exits (ggml-vulkan.cpp:16191 for the fallback, llama-context.cpp:2092 which grows and never shrinks). One 20k-token request strands ~19.9 GB. It is the daemon's single largest unreclaimable allocation and the reason 'restart between runs' kept being proposed. THE JUSTIFICATION FOR THE FLAG IS FALSE, measured not argued (tests/mtp_prefill_logits_spike.rs, 2026-08-27): model_slot.rs cites an upstream invariant that get_embeddings_pre_norm_ith errors with batch.logits[N] != true, but that error comes from output_resolve_row, which get_embeddings_nextn_ith calls ONLY on the masked path (llama-context.cpp:966); the unmasked path returns early at :954-960 indexing nextn rows densely by raw token position, and common_speculative initialises the MTP TARGET unmasked (speculative.cpp:1371 - the daemon logs set_embeddings_nextn: value = 1, masked = 0). On a 681-token prompt the pre-norm hidden states MTP actually consumes are BIT-IDENTICAL at every position with and without the flag, against a floor of 0e0, and 128 greedy tokens generate identically. WHY IT IS STILL DEFAULT OFF: the same spike found what source reading would not - the next-token logits shift by 1.46e-1 against a ZERO floor, because n_outputs_all going n -> 1 changes the output-gathering graph and therefore the float accumulation order for the row read. Small, did not flip a greedy decision over 128 tokens, but not nothing; it has to clear a byte-identity arm on a real composed report before becoming the default. The vendored precondition has a tripwire (the_mtp_target_context_is_still_initialised_unmasked) because a bump flipping that masked argument would make the change abort the daemon rather than error. Read in exactly one place (embedded::prompt_helpers::mtp_prefill_tail_logits_only). Reversal condition + evidence: sovereign/DEFAULTS_LEDGER.md. |
| `SOVEREIGN_MTP_QUARANTINE_DISABLE` | unset | guard | Kill-switch: disable the MTP quarantine (the guard that benches a model before trusting its MTP head). |
| `SOVEREIGN_NEXT_EDIT_FALLBACK` | off | experiment | =1/true serves the next-edit lane (POST /v1/edit_predictions) off the already-resident FAST slot when NO [models.edit] is configured, instead of serving nothing (install_fallback_next_edit_slot). Next-edit needs only a prompt dialect, not FIM marker tokens, so an ordinary chat model can serve it. MEASURED AND IT DID NOT HOLD (2026-08-07): the flag resolves through fast_path(), so on a box with an explicit [models].fast the answering model is the fast slot — a 4B there scored 14/30 useful (GM4 FAIL) at p95 2194ms, against 21/30 for the 35B-A3B chat primary and 19/30 / 828ms for a 1.5B specialist, same 60-case gym/next-edit/gen bank. Safe but not useful: 0 wrong edits in 17 fires. A bench number does not transfer down a model class. Marks the slot degraded=true, which drives the advice nudge on /status.inference.edit. An explicit [models.edit] always wins. STAYS OFF — opt-in only; users are pointed at `svrn setup --fim`. Ledger row: sovereign/DEFAULTS_LEDGER.md. |
| `SOVEREIGN_NEXT_EDIT_JOURNAL` | on | guard | =off/0/false stops the NEXT-EDIT journal stream only, leaving other streams recording (one record per POST /v1/edit_predictions, plus the editor's outcome report). Per-stream twin of SOVEREIGN_JOURNAL; the marker-file equivalent is `svrn journal next-edit off`. Every stream declares its own such var via JournalStream::disable_env. |
| `SOVEREIGN_PREFIX_STATE` | on | shipped | Caller-directed pinned-prefix full-state cache. Graduated default-on 2026-08-03 on a measured 1.30x through the production answer path (868.4s -> 669.0s, 2 reps/arm); the grounding gate is its only consumer. Opt out with =0. Worth most on archs where prefix_cache_gate vetoes ordinary partial-KV reuse. |
| `SOVEREIGN_PREFIX_STATE_MAX_MB` | 2048 | shipped | Per-slot byte cap on the pinned-state LRU. State files run ~64KB/token, so a 10K-token pin is ~650MB; this is what bounds the default-on pin's disk cost. |
| `SOVEREIGN_PREFIX_STATE_MIN` | code default | shipped | Minimum stable-prefix length (tokens) worth pinning. Below it, saving state costs more than the re-prefill it avoids. |
| `SOVEREIGN_RERANK_MODEL_PATH` | unset | experiment | Cross-encoder reranker GGUF path — installs the rerank slot [models.extra] otherwise declares. Default-inert but wired into the production daemon. DECIDED, do not re-raise: REJECTED 2026-08-04 (DEFAULTS_LEDGER.md — quality passed, killed on +2.8s TTFT + 4th resident slot + 60x memory fragility; dedup_by_source shipped instead); operator re-affirmed no-proving-arm 2026-08-14 (ECONOMY §7.7 addendum). Re-open only for a NEW integration shape (off-TTFT-path margins, no in-turn slot) or new evidence class (docs/archive/RERANK_EXPERIMENT.md). *(shadows `SetupConfig.models.extra`)* |
| `SOVEREIGN_SKIP_LOCAL_FIT_CHECK` | unset | guard | Skip the local fit check before joining a distributed load (rpc_distribution.rs). |
| `SOVEREIGN_SKIP_PER_DEVICE_FIT` | unset | guard | Skip the per-device fit check in the RPC byte-aware shard split. |
| `SOVEREIGN_SKIP_VRAM_CHECK` | unset | guard | Skip the model-fit VRAM check before load. |
| `SOVEREIGN_STRICT_VRAM_CHECK` | unset | guard | Make the preflight VRAM check strict (fail instead of warn). Same family as SOVEREIGN_SKIP_VRAM_CHECK — the fit-check knob cluster. |
| `SOVEREIGN_SYNTH_TEMP` | unset | experiment | Desktop synthesis temperature override. Near-synonym of SOVEREIGN_CONTENT_TEMPERATURE. |
| `SOVEREIGN_TENSOR_BUFT_OVERRIDE` | unset | experiment | Per-tensor placement at load, llama.cpp `-ot` syntax: `<regex>=<buffer-type>[,...]`, e.g. `per_layer_token_embd=CPU`. CPU is the only buffer type resolved, and it is the one that changes RESIDENCY: a tensor on the CPU buffer type is left pointing into the mmap'd GGUF instead of copied into a device buffer (llama-model-loader.cpp -> ggml_backend_tensor_alloc(buf_mmap, cur, data)), so it stays demand-paged from disk and EVICTABLE under pressure rather than pinned — pressure costs a page fault, not an OOM kill. Built for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's per_layer_token_embd, a single 26.8 GiB IQ4_NL n-gram table read 16 rows (1440 B) per token; measured NVMe marginal cost on RuggedFox is ~92 us against a ~25.6 ms token budget. Applied on LocalOnly/StreamSplit only — a distributed OwnedOverrides load derives its own -ot set from the shard plan and REFUSES to merge (logged at warn, not silently dropped). A malformed entry or unknown buffer type refuses the whole variable rather than half-applying. Read in one place: model_slot.rs::env_tensor_buft_overrides. |
| `SOVEREIGN_TENSOR_NO_HOST` | off | experiment | Bypass the device HOST buffer type for big local loads (llama.cpp `--no-host`), and with it the load-time prefetch: patch 0008 gates `init_mappings(!no_host)`, so this is also the only way to stop MAP_POPULATE making every CPU-placed weight resident before a single row is gathered. DEFAULT OFF BECAUSE IT WAS MEASURED HARMFUL ON THE CASE IT WAS WRITTEN FOR: on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next it turned the mmap-resident 26.8 GiB engram into an anonymous copy (RssAnon 8.85 -> 21.47 GiB, RssFile 0.29 -> 0.06 GiB) and the load OOM'd. Anonymous pages cannot be reclaimed; file-backed ones can. Kept as an opt-in because on a backend whose host buffer DOES accept the tensor's quant, CPU-placed weights really do land in pinned memory and this is the lever — measure RssAnon vs RssFile before turning it on. For placing ONE tensor on plain pageable CPU without this trade, use SOVEREIGN_TENSOR_BUFT_OVERRIDE instead. |

## mesh

| flag | default | status | purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SOVEREIGN_ADVERTISE_ADDR` | unset | shipped | Address this node advertises to mesh peers. |
| `SOVEREIGN_DISABLE_AUTO_COLLAB` | unset | guard | Kill-switch: disable auto-collaboration (peer ingest handoff) on the mesh. |

| `SOVEREIGN_DISABLE_PEER_INFERENCE` | unset | guard | Kill-switch: =1 keeps all inference local instead of load-balancing to mesh peers (solo bench runs, reproducibility). Read in sovereign-mesh/src/peer_inference.rs. |
| `SOVEREIGN_IROH` | unset | guard | Toggle for the iroh (no-VPN) mesh transport. *(shadows `SetupConfig.iroh.enabled`)* |
| `SOVEREIGN_IROH_RELAY_ONLY` | unset | guard | Force the iroh transport onto relay-only paths (what iroh.relay_urls/discovery express declaratively). *(shadows `SetupConfig.iroh.relay_urls`)* |
| `SOVEREIGN_JOIN_HOST` | unset | shipped | Mesh join target host override. |
| `SOVEREIGN_MESH_STRICT_AUTH` | off | guard | Refuse the pre-split gossip compat arm instead of falling back to it. OFF by default: `Mesh::gossip_authorized` falls through to comparing `invite_key_hash` whenever EITHER side's `mesh_secret` is zeroed, which is what makes the credential-split upgrade rolling rather than flag-day. That fallback is peer-selected — a caller omits the field and gets the weaker predicate — so once every node is upgraded it is pure attack surface. =1/true/on refuses those peers outright, but ONLY on a node whose own secret is set; a node that has not migrated would otherwise refuse every peer and self-partition. Read once via OnceLock in commonwealth-core (a value that changed mid-run would make `which predicate authorized this round` depend on when the round happened). Turning this on while any node is still pre-split PARTITIONS those nodes — that is the point, and it is why it is opt-in. Flip-to-default condition and review-by: sovereign/DEFAULTS_LEDGER.md. |
| `SOVEREIGN_PRIMARY_SIBLINGS` | unset | shipped | Distributed-inference primary's sibling set override. *(shadows `SetupConfig.models.primary_pool.copies`)* |
| `SOVEREIGN_RPC_DISCOVER` | unset | shipped | Discover half of the shared-model role. *(shadows `SetupConfig.shared_model.role`)* |
| `SOVEREIGN_RPC_HEADROOM` | unset | shipped | Per-device VRAM headroom for the byte-aware shard split (env wins when pre-set, setup_config.rs). *(shadows `SetupConfig.shared_model.headroom`)* |
| `SOVEREIGN_RPC_MIN_POOLED_GB` | unset | shipped | Minimum pooled VRAM before the shared model loads. *(shadows `SetupConfig.shared_model.min_pooled_gb`)* |
| `SOVEREIGN_RPC_QUORUM_ANCHORS` | unset | shipped | Anchor quorum for the pooled shared model. *(shadows `SetupConfig.shared_model.quorum_anchors`)* |
| `SOVEREIGN_RPC_SERVE` | unset | shipped | Anchor/host half of the shared-model role (env half of the config's role field). *(shadows `SetupConfig.shared_model.role`)* |
| `SOVEREIGN_RPC_SHARD_FETCH` | unset | shipped | Shard-fetch strategy for distributed model load. *(shadows `SetupConfig.shared_model.shard_fetch`)* |
| `SOVEREIGN_RPC_WORKER_PROCESS` | unset (in-process worker) | experiment | Serve the ggml RPC worker from a supervised child process instead of a thread in the daemon, so a peer-reachable GGML_ASSERT abort kills the child and not the process holding the mesh key. Accepts 1/true. |
| `SOVEREIGN_SCIP_LSP_TIER` | off | experiment | Reindexer warm tier: on each debounced save, ask the ALREADY-RUNNING rust-analyzer (via the lspmux shim, scripts/install-lspmux.sh) for the call edges rooted in the changed files, and ADD them to the code-intel graph. Closes the gap between the two existing tiers — the tree-sitter overlay refreshes symbol defs in milliseconds but can never see a cross-file call, and the full `rust-analyzer scip` export that can costs a cold analysis of all 54 crates (3m42s / 15.2 GB measured 2026-09-04) so it is gated behind a 900s cooldown. Strictly additive: the write is ScipGraph::add_call_edges_for, which executes no DELETE, so a still-loading analyzer answering `[]` costs nothing rather than emptying the edited file's edges. OFF by default because it spends a warm analyzer's time on the hot save path and the duty-cycle effect over a 30-minute editing window is not measured yet; flip-to-default condition and review-by in sovereign/DEFAULTS_LEDGER.md. |
| `SOVEREIGN_SEAT` | unset | shipped | Seat sessions only: makes the ambient notes read (inject-notes.py) pass include_operational=true, so seat coordination records are PRESENT instead of withheld (order seat-durable-rail UC-D4 inverse). Ordinary sessions never set it. |
| `SOVEREIGN_SHARED_MODEL_HOST_NODE_ID` | unset | shipped | Distributed-inference host node id override. *(shadows `SetupConfig.shared_model.host_node_id`)* |
| `SOVEREIGN_SHARED_MODEL_ID` | unset | shipped | Distributed-inference shared model id override (bootstrap.rs env-or-config). *(shadows `SetupConfig.shared_model.model_id`)* |
| `SOVEREIGN_WORKER_RUNNER` | unset | shipped | Distributed-inference worker runner selector. |

## retrieval

| flag | default | status | purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SOVEREIGN_ATLAS_EMBED_ATTRIBUTES` | off | experiment | Append a declared atom's `attributes` to its embed text (`attr: metal=silver; …`) so attribute questions have something to match. Atoms with no attributes render identically, so an undeclared corpus is unaffected. Flip conditions: sovereign/DEFAULTS_LEDGER.md. |
| `SOVEREIGN_ATLAS_GROUNDING` | on | shipped | Atlas graph-walk grounding: cosine seeds → BFS over typed edges → FTS-fetch evidence chunks. =0/false/off/no disables. |
| `SOVEREIGN_ATLAS_INCLUDE_DECLARED_CLAIMS` | off | experiment | Admit Claim atoms whose `claim_kind` names a DECLARED claim type into the atlas embedding bag. Narrower than SOVEREIGN_ATLAS_INCLUDE_CLAIMS; inert for a corpus that declares nothing. Flip conditions: sovereign/DEFAULTS_LEDGER.md. |
| `SOVEREIGN_ATOM_ENUM` | off | experiment | Enumeration-class questions get top-degree typed atoms injected as virtual chunks. Net-negative on focused enumeration (2026-06-04 bench); keep gated. |
| `SOVEREIGN_ATOM_ENUM_NOFILTER` | off | experiment | Ablation hatch: disable the enumeration-question classifier filter. |
| `SOVEREIGN_ATOM_ENUM_OVERVIEW` | on | shipped | Overview/summary questions inject the scoped corpus's atlas Claim atoms as virtual chunks. Independent of SOVEREIGN_ATOM_ENUM; question-shape detected, no LLM call. |
| `SOVEREIGN_ATOM_ENUM_POOL` | see helper | experiment | Atom-enumeration candidate-pool cap before ranking. |
| `SOVEREIGN_ATOM_ENUM_RANK` | rrf | experiment | Atom-enumeration ranking mode. |
| `SOVEREIGN_ATOM_ENUM_RELATIONS` | off | experiment | Include relation atoms in the enumeration. |
| `SOVEREIGN_ATOM_ENUM_SCORE` | see helper | shipped | Score stamped on enumerated virtual chunks. Shared with the shipped overview path — load-bearing. |
| `SOVEREIGN_ATOM_ENUM_TOPIC_GRIP` | 0.5 | shipped | Fraction of an overview question's TOPIC tokens (content tokens minus the overview framing) that a corpus's best atlas Claim must cover before ANY of that corpus's claims may be injected. Admission is per CORPUS, not per claim. Raising it toward 1.0 injects only on near-exact topical matches; 0.0 restores the pre-2026-08-05 behaviour where pool presence alone granted injection rights — which put 89 ARCH_PRINCIPLES chunks and a personal Obsidian vault into 14/14 SEP philosophy answers (audit D1). |
| `SOVEREIGN_ATOM_ENUM_TOPK` | see helper | shipped | How many enumerated atoms become virtual chunks. SHARED between the experimental entity path and the shipped overview path — load-bearing. |
| `SOVEREIGN_COMPACTION_DISABLE` | off | guard | History layer escape hatch: =1 disables dropped-history compaction. *(shadows `SetupConfig.memory.compaction`)* |
| `SOVEREIGN_CONV_PPR_WEIGHT` | off (0.0) | deprecated | Post-pipeline PPR rerank weight for conversation-corpus chunks. DEFAULT FLIPPED 0.25 -> 0.0 (OFF) 2026-08-04: a 180-question paired bank could not separate it from off (49-31 p=0.0567 alone; 64-43 p=0.0527 under the strongest retrieval config). It re-ranks in place and never adds a document — B-in-pool and source_ratio were identical to 4dp with it on and off — while rebuilding a per-conversation entity graph from SQL on every query and forcing GLiNER to run eagerly at ingest. Code kept and working; set a non-zero weight to re-enable. See DEFAULTS_LEDGER.md. |
| `SOVEREIGN_CORPUS_PREFILTER_TOPK` | off (unset); 12 is the calibrated K when set | experiment | Prune an UNSCOPED turn to the top-K query-relevant corpora before the fan-out, ranked by nearest-chunk cosine. Measured 2026-08-13 at 1000 corpora: ON is a 35% REGRESSION (22.1-22.4 s -> 29.7-30.6 s) because it ran once per fan-out, 4x per turn, each pass linear in n. SOVEREIGN_EXPANSION_SCOPE cuts it to one pass per turn. |
| `SOVEREIGN_COVERAGE_NEAR_SIM` | 0.55 | shipped | Similarity floor for the coverage probe's TopicUncovered/ClaimUncovered split. |
| `SOVEREIGN_COVERAGE_PROBE` | on | shipped | On gap/abstain turns: cross-corpus nearest-chunk-cosine probe classifying a gap as TopicUncovered vs ClaimUncovered. =0 disables. |
| `SOVEREIGN_DECOMP_DECAY` | 1.0 | experiment | Score decay applied to fanned-out sub-query hits (<1 = augment, never displace). |
| `SOVEREIGN_DEMAND_PLAN` | off | experiment | One fast-slot structured-output call plans the turn's demands (sub_queries, entities, stance contrast); feeds the epistemic demand set. |
| `SOVEREIGN_DEMAND_PLAN_FANOUT` | off | experiment | Fan the demand plan's sub_queries out into corpus search. Off after the 2026-07-19 A/B (2-3x slower for flat recall). |
| `SOVEREIGN_EPISTEMIC_STATE` | on | shipped | Post-pipeline per-turn epistemic ledger assembled into message metadata (pure collation, no model calls). =0 disables. |
| `SOVEREIGN_EXPANSION_SCOPE` | on | shipped | Scope every expansion fan-out (entity boost, decomp, title, demand-plan, graph-neighbor, and the spawned PPR + entity-obligations lanes) to the corpora the MAIN fan-out ranked highest, instead of re-searching every installed corpus. Also collapses the corpus prefilter to one pass per turn, since a scoped fan-out skips it. Default ON since 2026-08-13 (verdict 94f01eb2): retrieval slope 2.183 -> 0.849 s per 100 corpora, a 2.57x cut, with the SEP anchor byte-identical and the banks within noise (§8.4). =0/false/off/no disables. |
| `SOVEREIGN_EXPANSION_SCOPE_CORPORA` | 8 | experiment | How many CORPORA an expansion fan-out may search when SOVEREIGN_EXPANSION_SCOPE is on. The scale-vs-recall dial: lower is cheaper and narrower, higher is closer to unscoped. The unit is corpora, not chunks — a chunk budget let one corpus monopolise the scope and cost the wikipedia bank 3 sources / 4 facts. |
| `SOVEREIGN_FORENSIC` | off | experiment | Debug hatch: =1 enables audit_pipeline_stage composition snapshots between retrieval steps. |
| `SOVEREIGN_GRAPH_NEIGHBOR_EXPAND` | off | experiment | Axis-aware structural-graph one-hop expansion (per-entity axis neighbors + co-citation bridges). Wikipedia-specific, never promoted. |
| `SOVEREIGN_HISTORY_RETRIEVAL` | on | shipped | History layer: retrieval over prior conversation turns. =0 disables. |
| `SOVEREIGN_MERGE_SELECT` | on | shipped | Demand-aware merge composition (pins + per-entity demand slots + greedy diminishing-returns selector) replacing the cap/reserve/truncate heuristic pile. =0 restores the legacy stack. |
| `SOVEREIGN_META_BRIDGE` | off | experiment | Cross-corpus bridge boost: question entities matching a bridge topic pull the linked corpus's framing via typed edges. Built by `sovereign meta-atlas align`. |
| `SOVEREIGN_PPR_EXPAND` | on (dark without a reranker) | shipped | PPR walk + typed edges over the link graph propose answer-side articles; cross-encoder admission gate injects only CE-yes candidates. |
| `SOVEREIGN_QUERY_DECOMP` | off | experiment | Pure-Rust question decomposition; each sub-query gets its own focused retrieval pass. |

| `SOVEREIGN_TAVILY_API_KEY` | unset (Tavily disabled; DuckDuckGo is the zero-config fallback) | shipped | Tavily Search API key for the web-search orchestrator's Tavily backend. Read via svrnmesh_env("TAVILY_API_KEY") in the deep-research CLI port — the SVRNMESH_ prefix wins and the legacy SOVEREIGN_ spelling (the operator's shell line) is bridged at CLI startup, so either spelling works. Presence keys TavilyBackendImpl and makes tavily the deep-research web backend (the house prefer list's first external choice — best for citation-heavy synthesis); absence keeps DuckDuckGo. The value itself is never logged or echoed. |
